title: Projecting Current and Future Habitat for the European Ground Squirrel Using MaxEnt Modeling under Climate Change
abstract: Climate change and human activities are changing the places where different species live more and more quickly. The European ground squirrel (Spermophilus citellus) is a species at risk, and it plays a very important role in keeping grassland environments healthy. But right now, we still do not know clearly where this threatened species lives now and where it will live in the future as the climate changes. This study combined data from many different sources and used an improved Maximum Entropy (MaxEnt) model (the test AUC value is more than 0.87) to carefully study the current situation and future changes of the good living areas for this species. The results found that the number of people living in an area and isothermality are the main environmental factors that affect where this species lives. Future guesses show that the good living areas for it will keep getting smaller. This is especially true under the high-pollution SSP5-8.5 scenario. By the end of the century, this might lead to a total loss of more than 20% of its suitable living areas. At the same time, there will be a big drop in the number of high-quality living areas for the species. It is projected that the area where this species lives will have a big move to the north. This study points out that we badly need active and flexible management methods to protect this species. The species can survive only if the world works to cut greenhouse gases. The results give important scientific support for creating specific ways to protect the species.
problem: Conservation of the at-risk European ground squirrel is hindered by a lack of clear predictions for its current and future habitat, as previous studies have not fully integrated the combined effects of climate change, human activity, and other environmental drivers, thus hampering effective conservation planning.
method: This study uses an optimized Maximum Entropy (MaxEnt) model, integrating multi-source environmental data, to project the current and future suitable habitat distribution for the at-risk European ground squirrel under various climate change scenarios and to identify key environmental drivers influencing its survival.
task: The task is to project the current and future habitat suitability for the European ground squirrel under various climate change scenarios using an optimized Maximum Entropy (MaxEnt) model.
innovation: This paper integrates climatic, topographic, soil, and human-related data into a MaxEnt model to project the significant reduction and northward shift of suitable habitats for the endangered European ground squirrel under various climate change scenarios, providing a scientific basis for targeted conservation strategies.
